title: V1 inference cost-calculation method, v1alpha1
description: How a V1 inference cost figure is produced: which basis it carries, how a share of a machine is allocated to a workload, what happens to capacity nobody reserved, which time window it covers, where its prices came from, what units and precision it uses, what it does when an input is missing, and how much confidence it is allowed to claim. The method is committed as data so that every number in the worked example is arithmetic a test recomputes rather than a figure somebody typed. Nothing in this repository computes a cost record.

computationStatus.meaning: A repository tool, tools/cost_calculation, computes an estimated cost record by hand from one declared input document and a committed rate card. Nothing in a running system computes, emits, stores, or reads a cost record, and the only rate card committed here is synthetic, so every figure the tool has produced is economically meaningless.
computationStatus.producer: tools/cost_calculation, a repository tool run by hand that contacts no cluster, network, or telemetry store; which platform component computes and emits a cost record in a running system, and who owns it, is still not selected

bases.meaning: A figure taken from a provider's invoice or billing export for the period it covers.
bases.requires: an invoice or billing export from the party that charged for the capacity
bases.unreachableReason: This project has never been billed for anything. It runs on a local single-node cluster on a contributor's own machine, and no provider account, invoice, or billing export exists.
bases.notes: The word billing, and every synonym for it, belongs to this basis alone.

bases.meaning: A price applied to the capacity a workload reserved, whether or not it used any of it.
bases.requires: a price source, a node capacity declaration, and the workload's declared resource requests and replica count
bases.unreachableReason: V1 calculates the estimated basis only (ADR 0014 D1). An allocation and an estimate of one workload over one window answer different questions, and a producer able to emit both puts two numbers side by side where they are read as one. The arithmetic stays specified here and is demonstrated by the synthetic worked example, which no calculation produces.
bases.notes: Specified and not produced in V1. Every estimated record still carries what its workload reserved, so the reservation and the measured use sit side by side without being priced twice.

bases.meaning: A price applied to observed utilisation over the window rather than to what was reserved.
bases.requires: a price source and measured processor, memory, or accelerator utilisation integrated over the window
bases.notes: The only basis V1 calculates, since ADR 0014. Measured use reaches a calculation only as values supplied in its input, with the evidence class they came from; nothing in this repository reads a utilisation series from a running system.

basisRules: A record carries exactly one basis.
Amounts on different bases are never summed into one total.
A record whose basis is not `actual` carries no provider invoice reference, and no field that would let one be inferred.

allocationMethods.meaning: A workload is charged for the share of a node's allocatable capacity that it reserved: its processor and memory requests, multiplied by its replica count, multiplied by the window length.
allocationMethods.deferralReason: It produces the allocated basis, which V1 does not produce (ADR 0014 D1). ADR 0007 D2 selected it while no measured use existed, and its reasoning is kept there.
allocationMethods.honestCost: A workload that reserves four processor cores and uses a tenth of one is charged the same as a workload that uses all four. That is correct capacity accounting and useless efficiency accounting, and it is a property of the method rather than a defect in it.

allocationMethods.meaning: A workload is charged for the share of the node's capacity it was measured to use, integrated over the window.
allocationMethods.whyChosen: The V1-S4-004 scenario matrix committed measured processor and memory use of a declared local experiment, so the deferral ADR 0007 D2 recorded is deleted rather than a method invented (ADR 0014 D2). It is the method the estimated basis needs.
allocationMethods.honestCost: It rewards a workload for reserving capacity it does not use, which is a cost the reserving workload has already imposed on everything else on the node.

allocationMethods.meaning: A node's cost is divided between workloads in proportion to the requests each one served.
allocationMethods.honestCost: It makes one workload's unit cost depend on how busy its neighbours were. A workload whose traffic halves while nothing else changes appears to double in price, which is a statement about the neighbours rather than about the workload.

residualTreatments.meaning: Capacity no workload reserved is reported as its own line, attributed to the environment rather than to any workload.
residualTreatments.why: It is the only treatment under which the workload lines and the residual add up to the node, so a reader can see both the unit costs and the fact that most of the machine was idle. Making the idle share visible is the point: it is usually the largest number on the page.

residualTreatments.meaning: Unreserved capacity is divided between workloads in proportion to what each reserved.
residualTreatments.why: It makes a workload's unit cost depend on how empty the machine was, so the same workload doing the same work changes price when an unrelated workload is removed. It also hides idle capacity in numbers that look like workload costs.

residualTreatments.meaning: Unreserved capacity is not costed at all.
residualTreatments.why: The workload lines then sum to less than the machine, and the gap is invisible. This is the treatment that makes a unit cost look defensible while the environment quietly costs several times the sum of its parts.

sharedCostRules.statement: Node capacity that no workload reserved is reported as an `unallocated` line attributed to the environment.
sharedCostRules.why: A cost model whose parts do not sum to the whole is a cost model whose gap nobody has to explain.

sharedCostRules.statement: Storage and other resources whose lifecycle is longer than a release - the model cache above all - are attributed to the prerequisite layer, not to the workload that happens to mount them.
sharedCostRules.why: The model cache deliberately outlives the release that uses it, so that uninstalling does not force a re-download over a transport whose downloader does not validate certificates. A cost that survives the workload is not the workload's cost, and charging it to a workload would make deleting the workload look like a saving it is not.

sharedCostRules.statement: Cluster control-plane and platform overhead is environment cost. It is neither spread across workloads nor omitted.
sharedCostRules.why: It is real, it is shared, and dividing it produces per-workload numbers that move when the workload count changes.

windowRules.interval: half-open: the window includes its start instant and excludes its end instant, so adjacent windows neither overlap nor leave a gap
windowRules.format: RFC 3339 with an explicit Z offset
windowRules.alignmentRule: A window of the default length starts on the hour.
windowRules.shapeChangeRule: If a workload's resource requests, accelerator count, or replica count changed inside a window, the window is split at the change and one record is produced per segment. The method has no defensible way to average an allocation across a shape change, and averaging one would produce a number that describes no state the system was ever in.
windowRules.partialWindowRule: A workload that existed for part of the window is charged for the part it existed, and the record records the window as incomplete.
windowRules.clockSource: the producing component's own clock, recorded in the record; no clock is reconciled against any other

units.meaning: One processor core reserved or used for one hour.
units.definition: Kubernetes processor quantities are millicores; 1000m is one core. A quantity is converted to cores by dividing by 1000 before any price is applied.

units.meaning: One gibibyte of memory reserved or used for one hour.
units.definition: One gibibyte is 2^30 bytes. Kubernetes memory quantities are binary, so 2Gi is 2 gibibytes and never 2 gigabytes; reading one as the other introduces a 7.4 per cent error in every memory line, silently.

units.meaning: One gibibyte of persistent storage claimed for one hour.
units.definition: Separate from memory because it is priced separately and because its lifecycle is different: a claim survives the release that mounted it.

units.meaning: One accelerator device reserved or used for one hour.
units.definition: Accelerators are whole devices in V1. There is no fractional device, no time-slicing, and no multi-instance partitioning, because the workload contract allocates whole devices by count.

units.meaning: One inference request accepted by the platform, whatever its outcome.
units.definition: A refused request is still a request: it consumed the capacity that refused it. Counting only successes would make a failing workload look cheap.

units.meaning: One token as counted by the serving runtime's own tokeniser.
units.definition: Input and output tokens are counted separately and summed only for a combined denominator. No token count is derived from a character or word count.
Used for durations that describe a window rather than a reservation, and never priced directly.
Replica counts and device counts. Never fractional.
RFC 3339 with an explicit Z offset. UTC only.

units.meaning: A name that identifies a thing rather than measures one.
units.definition: Carried through to the record unchanged and never arithmetic.

units.meaning: An amount of money in the record's declared currency.
units.definition: A decimal string at the record scale. One currency per record.

units.meaning: A dimensionless proportion between zero and one.
units.definition: A decimal string at the ratio scale. Never a percentage in the data; a document may render one.

money.roundingPoint: once, at the end of a computation; never on an intermediate value
money.currencyRule: One currency per record, declared in the record. No conversion, no exchange rate, and no mixed-currency total.
money.whyNotFloat: Binary floating point cannot represent a tenth exactly. Summing hundreds of minute-level allocations in a float drifts, and a cost model that disagrees with itself on re-run is worse than no cost model.
money.whyNotMinorUnits: Rounding to a currency's minor unit is a billing operation, and V1 never bills. Records keep six decimal places so that a fraction of a cent per record is neither rounded into existence nor out of it.

priceSourceClasses.meaning: A published rate card from a named provider, captured at a stated version and date.
requirements: the captured values committed as data rather than fetched

priceSourceClasses.meaning: A contracted rate that differs from the list price.
requirements: a contract reference the record may not quote
an authorised holder of that contract

priceSourceClasses.meaning: A local machine's purchase price, power, and lifetime reduced to an hourly rate.
Invented rates that exist to demonstrate the arithmetic.
requirements: the artifact says inside itself that it is synthetic

priceSources.name: Synthetic illustrative rate card
priceSources.scope: the worked example and the calculation fixtures in this repository, and nothing else
priceSources.notes: Every rate here is invented. The numbers were chosen to be round enough that the worked example's arithmetic can be followed by hand, and they correspond to no provider, no region, no contract, and no machine. A record priced from this source is structurally valid and economically meaningless, and the confidence rules cap it at none for exactly that reason.

priceSourceRules.statement: Every price a record uses comes from a source committed to this repository. Nothing retrieves a price over a network while computing.
priceSourceRules.why: A price that moves makes a cost figure irreproducible, and a re-run that produces a different number is not a re-run. It also makes the computation depend on an external service being reachable and honest.

priceSourceRules.statement: A record names the price source identifier, its version, and its effective date. A source without all three cannot be cited.
priceSourceRules.why: Two records that disagree are either a change in usage or a change in price, and without the version there is no way to tell which.

priceSourceRules.statement: A synthetic rate card declares its class inside the artifact, not in the directory it sits in or the document that links to it.
priceSourceRules.why: The same rule the mock serving boundary already applies: a label that lives outside the artifact does not survive the artifact being copied out of it.

confidenceLevels.meaning: The amount is structurally valid and economically meaningless. It demonstrates the arithmetic and may not be read as what anything costs.
A real price applied to declared capacity. It says what the reserved capacity would be charged at that rate, and nothing about what was used.
A real price applied to measured utilisation over a complete window.
Taken from an invoice for the period it covers.

confidenceRules.why: Only a bill establishes what was charged. Everything else is a model of it.
An allocation states what was reserved. Whether any of it was used is a question it does not answer.
A record labelled estimated whose utilisation inputs are all declared is an allocation wearing a better word.
The arithmetic can be checked; the prices are invented, so the amount describes nothing.
A window missing part of its data produces a total that is lower than the truth by an unknown amount, which is the direction that flatters.
An allocation averaged across a change in reservation describes a machine state that never existed.

confidenceDerivation: The confidence of a record is the lowest ceiling among the rules whose conditions all hold for it. It is never asserted by the producer and never raised by hand; a record whose declared confidence differs from the derived one fails the suite.

inputs.name: period.start
inputs.coverageNote: The producing component's own clock. Nothing measures it.
inputs.question: When does the accounting period begin?

inputs.name: period.end
inputs.coverageNote: The producing component's own clock. Nothing measures it.
inputs.question: When does it end, exclusively?

inputs.name: capacity.cpuCores
inputs.coverageNote: No metric reports node allocatable capacity, and nothing in this repository reads it from a cluster.
inputs.question: How much processor capacity is there to allocate from?

inputs.name: capacity.memoryGibibytes
inputs.coverageNote: No metric reports node allocatable capacity, and nothing in this repository reads it from a cluster.
inputs.question: How much memory is there to allocate from?

inputs.name: capacity.acceleratorDevices
inputs.coverageNote: No metric reports accelerator capacity, and the one executed serving trial this project holds ran on a processor with no accelerator at all.
inputs.question: How many accelerator devices are there to allocate from?

inputs.name: spec.resources.cpu
inputs.coverageNote: Read from the validated workload document, which requires it in every environment and refuses a workload that omits it.
inputs.question: How much processor capacity did this workload reserve per replica?

inputs.name: spec.resources.memory
inputs.coverageNote: Read from the validated workload document.
inputs.question: How much memory did this workload reserve per replica?

inputs.name: spec.resources.accelerator.count
inputs.coverageNote: Read from the validated workload document.
inputs.question: How many accelerator devices did this workload reserve per replica?

inputs.name: deployment.replicas
inputs.coverageNote: The replica count in force during the window. The workload document declares a minimum and a maximum, which are a range and not a number; a record uses the count actually deployed and splits the window if it changed.
inputs.question: How many copies of this reservation existed during the window?

inputs.name: cost.priceSourceId
inputs.coverageNote: Committed data. Never fetched.
inputs.question: Which rate card produced these amounts, at which version and date?

inputs.name: usage.requests
inputs.coverageNote: The platform counts the requests it receives. This is the counter the selected serving runtime does not expose and the platform produces itself, which the telemetry catalog already records. A calculation takes it from a committed bounded experiment record (ADR 0013), typed into the calculation input by hand (ADR 0014 D3); no reader in this repository derives it from that record.
inputs.question: How many requests is this amount being divided by?

inputs.name: usage.inputTokens
inputs.coverageNote: Carried on the token counter under the input direction. The selected runtime does expose a prompt-token counter, so this is one of the few usage inputs with a real source behind it, once anything scrapes it. A calculation takes it from a committed bounded experiment record (ADR 0013), typed into the calculation input by hand (ADR 0014 D3); no reader in this repository derives it from that record.
inputs.question: How many input tokens did this workload process?

inputs.name: usage.outputTokens
inputs.coverageNote: Carried on the same counter under the output direction. A calculation takes it from a committed bounded experiment record (ADR 0013), typed into the calculation input by hand (ADR 0014 D3); no reader in this repository derives it from that record.
inputs.question: How many output tokens did it produce?

inputs.name: usage.cpuSeconds
inputs.coverageNote: The named counter is process-scoped and belongs to the platform process, and no catalog signal reports container or node processor use. A calculation takes this input instead from the node's cgroup processor counters sampled beside a declared local experiment: the counter's increase between the samples bounding the window (ADR 0014 D3). It is typed into the calculation input by hand, and no reader in this repository takes it from the samples.
inputs.question: How much processor time did this workload actually consume?

inputs.name: usage.memoryByteSeconds
inputs.coverageNote: The named signal is an instantaneous gauge of the platform process. A calculation takes this input instead from the node's cgroup memory working-set readings sampled beside a declared local experiment, integrated trapezoidally between consecutive samples inside the window and never extrapolated past the first or last (ADR 0014 D3). It is typed into the calculation input by hand, and no reader in this repository integrates the samples.
inputs.question: How much memory did this workload actually hold, over time?

inputs.name: usage.acceleratorSeconds
inputs.coverageNote: No metric in the telemetry catalog reports accelerator use, and no accelerator has ever been used by this project.
inputs.question: How much accelerator time did this workload consume?

inputs.name: usage.readySeconds
inputs.coverageNote: Derived by integrating a readiness gauge, with the same store and interpolation problem as memory. A workload that was not ready still reserved its capacity, so this input changes no amount; it exists so that a record can say how much of the window the reservation was able to serve at all.
inputs.question: For how much of the window could this reservation answer a request?

inputs.name: identity.workloadId
inputs.coverageNote: A declared catalog attribute.
inputs.question: Which workload is this record about?

inputs.name: identity.ownerId
inputs.coverageNote: A declared catalog attribute.
inputs.question: Who is accountable for this cost?

inputs.name: identity.tenantId
inputs.coverageNote: A declared catalog attribute, classed tenant-attributable, which is why it may not appear in a committed record.
inputs.question: Whose activity does this cost attribute to?

inputs.name: identity.environment
inputs.coverageNote: A declared catalog attribute.
inputs.question: Is this a development host, and may this figure be cited as anything else?

inputs.name: identity.modelId
inputs.coverageNote: A declared catalog attribute.
inputs.question: Which model was this capacity reserved for?

inputs.name: identity.runtimeId
inputs.coverageNote: A declared catalog attribute.
inputs.question: Which serving runtime held it?

inputs.name: recordId
inputs.coverageNote: The catalog registered this attribute and deferred it, so that the first code to need the name would adopt the agreed one. A calculation input declares the value and the record carries it; no telemetry does, because nothing emits a cost record.
inputs.question: Which cost record is this, so that a request can be tied back to it?

outputs.name: reserved.cpuCoreHours
outputs.question: How much processor capacity did this workload hold out of circulation?

outputs.name: reserved.memoryGibibyteHours
outputs.question: How much memory did it hold out of circulation?

outputs.name: reserved.acceleratorDeviceHours
outputs.question: How many device-hours did it hold?

outputs.name: cost.amount
outputs.formula: reservedCpuCoreHours * rate(cpu-core-hour) + reservedMemoryGibibyteHours * rate(memory-gibibyte-hour) + reservedAcceleratorDeviceHours * rate(accelerator-device-hour)
outputs.question: What does the capacity this workload reserved cost at the stated rates?

outputs.name: cost.amount
outputs.formula: (cpuSeconds * rate(cpu-core-hour) + memoryByteSeconds / 2^30 * rate(memory-gibibyte-hour) + acceleratorSeconds * rate(accelerator-device-hour)) / 3600, with the accelerator term absent when the workload reserves no device
outputs.question: What did the processor, memory, and accelerator time this workload was measured using come to at the committed rates?

outputs.name: capacity.amount
outputs.formula: (allocatableCpuCores * rate(cpu-core-hour) + allocatableMemoryGibibytes * rate(memory-gibibyte-hour) + allocatableAcceleratorDevices * rate(accelerator-device-hour)) * windowHours
outputs.question: What does the whole machine cost for this window?

outputs.name: unallocated.amount
outputs.question: What is the machine costing for capacity nobody reserved?

outputs.name: prerequisite.amount
outputs.question: What do the resources that outlive a release cost for this window?

outputs.name: derived.amountPerHour
outputs.question: At what hourly rate did this amount accrue over the window it covers? It describes that window and projects nothing beyond it.

outputs.name: derived.shareOfNodeCapacity
outputs.question: How much of the machine is this workload holding?

outputs.name: derived.costPerThousandRequests
outputs.question: What does a thousand requests cost, at this reservation and this traffic?

outputs.name: derived.costPerMillionTokens
outputs.question: What does a million tokens cost, at this reservation and this traffic?

denominatorRules.statement: A unit cost is reported only when its denominator reaches the stated minimum, and a reported unit cost always carries the denominator it was divided by.
denominatorRules.why: A cost per thousand requests computed from four requests is a statement about four requests wearing the units of a rate. Carrying the denominator makes that visible without having to know the rule.
denominatorRules.honesty: Both minimums are declared, not derived. No analysis produced 100 or 10,000; they are round numbers chosen to be obviously too small to publish from, and a better-founded threshold would need traffic this project has never had.

missingDataRules.statement: An input that is not available is recorded as unavailable with a reason, and every output that depends on it is null. An unavailable input is never substituted with zero, with a default, or with a value from another window.
missingDataRules.why: Zero is a measurement. Writing zero tokens where there is no token telemetry produces a record that says the workload processed nothing, and a cost per million tokens computed from it would be a division by a fiction.
missingDataRules.completenessRule: Every record lists the inputs that were unavailable. A record with no unavailable inputs says so explicitly rather than omitting the field.

missingDataReasons.meaning: No component emits the signal this input would come from, or no collector reads it.
The serving runtime does not publish the quantity, and no platform component derives it.
The denominator exists but is below the declared minimum for a unit cost.
The value exists but belongs to a period this record does not cover.
Two sources disagree and the method has no rule for choosing between them.
Nothing computes this record, so the field has never been populated by anything.

recordShape.note: This is the method's output shape, published here as part of the method. It is not a contract: no schema for it is published under contracts/, because nothing in a running system produces or consumes one, and the contract package adds a schema when the capability behind it exists rather than in advance. The repository tool that computes a record by hand validates every record it writes against these fields.

prohibitions.statement: An amount whose basis is not actual is never described as billing, an invoice, a charge, or spend, and never carries a provider invoice reference.
prohibitions.rationale: The distance between a model of a cost and a cost is the whole subject of this record, and one word closes it.

prohibitions.statement: A total is computed within one basis. Two amounts on different bases are two numbers.
prohibitions.rationale: A sum across bases produces a figure that is neither measured nor reserved, and nothing downstream can tell which half it should distrust.

prohibitions.statement: Every price comes from a source committed to this repository. No computation retrieves a price over a network.
prohibitions.rationale: A moving price makes a re-run produce a different number, and a number that cannot be reproduced cannot be evidence.

prohibitions.statement: A synthetic rate card declares its class inside the artifact.
prohibitions.rationale: A label that lives in the directory name does not survive the file being copied out of it.

prohibitions.statement: A record's confidence is the lowest ceiling among the applicable rules, recomputed rather than read.
prohibitions.rationale: Confidence typed by the producer is confidence the producer wanted.

prohibitions.statement: A missing input is null and carries a reason; every null output has a reason and every reason belongs to a null output or a null input.
prohibitions.rationale: Zero is a measurement, and substituting it turns an absent signal into a claim that nothing happened.

prohibitions.statement: Capacity nobody reserved is its own line, and the workload lines plus the residual equal the machine exactly.
prohibitions.rationale: A model whose parts do not sum to the whole hides the largest number on the page.

prohibitions.statement: A reported unit cost states the request or token count it was divided by, and is null below the declared minimum.
prohibitions.rationale: A rate computed from four requests looks exactly like a rate computed from four million.

prohibitions.statement: Every amount and rate in the committed method is a decimal string at a declared scale.
prohibitions.rationale: A tenth has no binary representation, and a cost model that disagrees with itself on re-run is not a cost model.

prohibitions.statement: No record committed to this repository carries a tenant identifier, in the worked example or anywhere else.
prohibitions.rationale: The telemetry catalog classes a tenant identifier as tenant-attributable, which has no permitted placement in a committed evidence record: such a record is public and permanent, and a tenant list with a retention window of forever is not what anybody intended by adding an attribution field.

prohibitions.statement: Resources whose lifecycle is longer than a release are attributed to the prerequisite layer, not to a workload.
prohibitions.rationale: The model cache outlives the release on purpose. Charging it to a workload makes deleting the workload look like a saving that does not occur.

prohibitions.statement: Each input either names a signal the telemetry catalog declares, or records that no source exists and why.
prohibitions.rationale: An input with an unstated source is an input somebody will assume is available.

prohibitions.statement: V1 publishes this method and a synthetic worked example. It publishes no figure for what running an inference workload costs.
prohibitions.rationale: A cost per thousand requests is a throughput figure with a price attached, and the project boundaries forbid publishing a throughput figure. The prohibition is not a formality here: dividing an hourly reservation by an hour of traffic publishes that traffic.

prohibitions.statement: A record never averages an allocation across a change in resource requests or replica count.
prohibitions.rationale: The average describes a machine state that never existed, and it is indistinguishable in the output from a state that did. The calculation refuses an input that declares a change inside its window. A change nobody declared is caught by review alone, which is why this rule stays marked as review.

prohibitions.statement: The only basis V1 reaches is estimated. Actual needs an invoice, and allocated is specified and not produced.
prohibitions.rationale: ADR 0014 D1. One basis per calculation means an estimate and an allocation of the same workload and window never appear side by side to be read, or summed, as one number.

prohibitions.statement: A calculation input asking for the actual or the allocated basis is refused before any figure is written, with the reason the method gives.
prohibitions.rationale: A basis that is unreachable in data and reachable in code is reachable.

prohibitions.statement: A calculation reads a price only from a source committed in this method, and refuses one that is fetched, unversioned, undated, priced in a float, negative, or incomplete, or synthetic without saying so.
prohibitions.rationale: ADR 0007 D5 and D6, applied where a price is used rather than only where it is stored.

prohibitions.statement: A calculation input names the evidence class its usage values came from, and only a measured class lets a record state that its utilisation was measured.
prohibitions.rationale: ADR 0014 D3. Synthetic usage priced on the estimated basis would otherwise derive the confidence of a measurement.

prohibitions.statement: Every record a calculation writes carries every required field of the published record shape, at its declared type, and no field a committed record may not carry.
prohibitions.rationale: ADR 0007 D10 publishes the shape as part of the method rather than as a contract, so the method is what a record is checked against.

workedExample.warning: Every number in this example is invented. The capacities, the reservations, the traffic, and above all the prices correspond to no machine, no provider, and no measurement this project has ever taken. It exists to show that the arithmetic closes and that a missing input produces a null rather than a zero.

prerequisite.note: The model cache claim outlives any release that mounts it, so its cost belongs to the environment's prerequisite layer and to no workload.

records.note: The traffic figures are synthetic and exist only to give the unit costs a denominator. The three unavailable inputs are exactly the ones an estimated basis would need, which is why this record is allocated.

This record exists to exercise the two missing-data paths. Forty requests is below the declared minimum, so the request unit cost is null rather than a rate; no token telemetry exists for a mock profile, so the token unit cost is null rather than zero. The amount itself is unaffected, because an allocation does not depend on traffic.

counterfactuals.note: What the first workload would have been charged had the residual been divided in proportion to what each workload reserved. It is stated as data rather than prose so that the argument against this treatment is arithmetic the suite recomputes, and not a ratio somebody estimated.

What the first workload would have been charged had the residual been dropped. The amount is unchanged, which is the point: discarding leaves the workload lines identical and the machine unaccounted for.

unallocated.note: Sixty-nine per cent of the machine was reserved by nobody. It is the largest line in the example, and every treatment other than reporting it separately would have hidden it inside a unit cost.

totals.note: The two workload lines plus the unallocated line equal the node capacity line exactly. The environment total adds the prerequisite storage line, which belongs to no workload.

telemetryMapping.statement: Every usage and identity input names the telemetry signal that would supply it, or records that no signal exists. A test checks each named signal against the committed telemetry catalog, so an input cannot claim a source the catalog does not declare.

gaps.statement: The catalog's two process metrics describe the emitting process, not a container or a node, and the local cluster runs no metrics server.
gaps.consequence: No catalog signal supplies the estimated basis. It is reachable only from the node cgroup samples of a declared local experiment, typed into a calculation input by hand (ADR 0014 D3), and the observed-utilisation-share method has no telemetry source.

gaps.statement: No metric in the catalog reports accelerator use, and no accelerator has been used by this project.
gaps.consequence: An accelerator line can be allocated from a declaration and never estimated from use.

gaps.statement: The API emits these signals and the release-scoped collector scrapes them, but no durable store keeps what it scrapes and no component reads them into a cost calculation.
gaps.consequence: A calculation takes request and token counts from a committed bounded experiment record, typed in by hand. No usage input is read from a running system.

openQuestions.statement: Which provider rate cards a comparison against hosted capacity would be priced from, at which regions and versions.
openQuestions.why: No provider is selected and no account exists. Committing a rate card for a provider this project has never used would publish a number with the shape of evidence and none of the substance.

openQuestions.statement: Which platform component computes and emits a cost record in a running system, and who owns it.
openQuestions.status: not decided, and not this record's to decide
openQuestions.why: The resource-ownership inventory assigns this to nobody, and the same inventory already leaves a telemetry collector unowned. A method that quietly nominated an owner would answer an architecture question in a cost document. A repository tool that computes a record by hand from a declared input (ADR 0014) does not answer it: it runs in no cluster and emits nothing.

limitations.statement: No platform component computes a cost record. A repository tool computes one by hand from a declared input document, and nothing in a running system computes, emits, stores, or reads one.
The actual basis is unreachable. This project has no provider account, no invoice, and no billing export, so nothing here has ever been compared against what anybody was charged.
Every rate committed here is invented. Amounts computed from it are structurally valid and economically meaningless, and the confidence rules cap them at none for that reason.

There is no metrics server, and no collector keeps a durable utilisation series. Measured processor and memory use reaches a calculation only as values typed in by hand from a committed bounded experiment, and no reader in this repository integrates them from its samples.

Allocation by reservation charges a workload for capacity it did not use. That is the definition of the method rather than a defect in it, and it makes these figures capacity accounting rather than efficiency accounting.

The estimated basis prices what a workload was measured using, so capacity it reserved and left idle lands on the unallocated line rather than on its record. That is the cost ADR 0007 D2 named for observed use, and the reservation each record carries is what keeps it visible.
Node allocatable capacity is a declared input. Nothing in this repository reads it from a cluster, so a record can be produced against a machine that does not exist.
The minimum denominators of 100 requests and 10,000 tokens are declared, not derived. No analysis produced them.

Cost per thousand requests is an amount divided by a window of traffic, which publishes the traffic. ADR 0013 now permits a bounded traffic figure from a declared local experiment; ADR 0007 D11 still publishes no cost figure, so the method's unit costs exist here only on synthetic prices.

A contributor's own machine has no hourly price. Hardware amortisation, power, and lifetime assumptions would each be a guess, and multiplying four guesses produces a number with more decimal places than meaning. That is why the only committed rate card is labelled synthetic rather than local.
One currency per record, no exchange rates, and no mixed-currency totals. A multi-currency estimate needs a rate source with a date, which is a second price-source problem this method does not solve.
Network egress, load balancing, and ingress are not priced. The local cluster ships no ingress controller and no load balancer, which the ownership inventory already records as an open cost.
The worked example's traffic figures are chosen numbers. No request in it was served and no token in it was generated.

Every usage value in a calculation input is typed in by whoever prepares it. The calculation checks its evidence class, its shape, and that it fits within the node's declared capacity for the window, and cannot check that it matches the evidence it came from.
